xwhatsapp-strokecopylinkgoogleAdd Al Jazeera on GoogleinfoThe Russian cargo vessel Sparta II is shown on fire off the southern coast of Finland after being struck by two drones on Saturday [Finnish Border Guard photo]By David Mac Dougall and ReutersPublished On 21 Nov 202621 Nov 2026The crew of a Russian ship in the Gulf of Finland, hit by drones likely launched by Ukraine, is being evacuated into life rafts and a rescue boat.

Finnish authorities say the Sparta II has links to Russia’s armed forces and has drifted into territorial waters off Finland’s southern coast.

“There is a fire on board the ship. The situation does not pose a danger to maritime traffic or people. A restricted area has been set up around the site to ensure safety,” the Finnish Border Guard said in a statement, adding that it is in “close international cooperation” with neighbouring countries, including contact with Russia’s maritime rescue authorities.

On Saturday morning, Finland’s Ministry of Defence said its forces detected a drone attack on a Russian vessel in international waters, with initial reports saying the ship had sustained damage. Finnish Border Guard units were dispatched to the scene, and a photograph taken by a Finnish patrol plane showed flames and thick smoke coming from the rear of the ship.

The attack happened west of Gogland Island, off the coast of the Finnish town of Loviisa, and Finland quickly implemented temporary air and sea traffic restrictions in the eastern part of the gulf.

A Russian helicopter has since violated Finnish airspace, venturing more than 4km into Finnish territory.

“The suspected airspace violation is possibly related to rescue or tracking operations of a damaged cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland. The Defence Forces and the Border Guard are handling the situation in cooperation with other authorities,” said Minister of Defence Antti Hakkanen.

By Saturday afternoon the Finnish Defence Forces said the strike was likely carried out by Ukraine. Earlier, Finland’s Prime Minister Petteri Orpo wrote on X that “war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity. The Finnish authorities are handling the situation in the Gulf of Finland, where a drone strike has hit a Russian merchant vessel. Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor.”

Finland’s Border Guard said the Sparta II is known to have links to Russia’s armed forces. The roll-on-roll-off ship was built in the year 2000 and sails under a Russian flag, according to the vesselfinder.com website.

“At the moment, ⁠⁠⁠⁠there is no confirmed information about ⁠⁠⁠⁠what cargo is on ⁠⁠⁠⁠board, but ⁠⁠⁠⁠it cannot be ruled out that there ‌‌‌‌is military materiel on board,” Iljin said.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Russia’s Leningrad region, said damage to the ship had yet to be fully assessed.

“Three nautical miles from the Russian Federation’s border, a cargo vessel bound for Kaliningrad was attacked by two drones,” he wrote on the messaging app Max.

Kaliningrad’s Governor Alexey Besprozvannykh said supplies to the Russian exclave were not at risk.

One of the major risks of attacking any vessel is environmental damage if it leaks or sinks, a scenario that Baltic Sea nations treat with high importance. That risk is “further amplified by the poor state of some of the so-called ‘Shadow Fleet’ tankers” that Russia operates, according to Robin Haggblom, senior adviser for Risk Intelligence and an expert in Finnish maritime issues.

“Actions to prevent environmental damage has also been emphasised in Finnish Border Guard communication regarding this event. Luckily in this case, we don’t yet have ice coverage in the Gulf of Finland, which would impact any oil spill recovery efforts that may be needed,” Haggblom told Al Jazeera.

The narrow and shallow waters of the Baltic Sea are some of the most crowded shipping lanes in the world. The Helsinki to Tallinn ferry route had 7.5m passenger crossings last year. Other passenger routes link Baltic ports and capital cities, and cargo vessels and military shipping contribute to the total number of vessels in the relatively small body of water.

So if Ukraine is using drones – maritime or aerial – to hit Russian ships, could there be any risks to civilian vessels?

“There obviously always is a risk of collateral damage. However, so far Ukraine does seem to be taking a number of steps to minimise the risks involved, with the Sparta II for example apparently having been identified and hit a handful of kilometres from Russian waters,” added expert Haggblom.

Earlier this month, Finland’s military said it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland, which Ukraine took credit for. Helsinki later said it had raised concerns with Kyiv about strikes in the area.

“It is the same with the strike on the Russian corvette earlier, where it is reported the Ukrainians were able to pick it out and target that specific vessel among perhaps a dozen other ships. There are also unconfirmed indications that Sparta II was targeted specifically, and not just as a general Russia-associated merchant vessel,” Häggblom added.

Ukraine and Russia have attacked each other’s shipping throughout the war, mostly in the Black Sea.
